features.name: CLI framework: Qt-free dispatch, enrichment-cli/1 envelope, cli_commands registry
verified_by: tests/test_cli_registry.py (synthetic; 249 passed with tests/test_help_docs.py in 2.1 s on 2026-11-11)
109 scratch probes on a synthetic sample project, stdin closed: no traceback, one JSON document per --json call (synthetic)
remaining: Failure-envelope `command` label is inconsistent (F-D04).
Status vocabulary has undocumented values `ok`, `too-broad` (F-D06); owner decision.
Usage errors print one line without the usage block (audit CLI-15, still open).
`correlate --save-snapshot` uses Path.write_text: CRLF on Windows and not atomic (src/patchtrace/cli.py:490; audit CLI-13, still open; Windows behaviour UNVERIFIED).
`patchtrace kb` with no action prints help and exits 0 (src/patchtrace/cli_commands/kb.py:16) while every other verb group exits 2.
No `--version` (`patchtrace --version` exits 2: 'the following arguments are required: command').

defects.summary: The `command` field of a failure envelope differs from the success envelope for registry verbs and for parse failures.
defects.failure_scenario: `patchtrace build-env show MISSING --json` prints command 'build-env' (success prints 'build-env show'); `patchtrace pilot why P --candidate x --json` prints command 'patchtrace'; `patchtrace secondary binexport-check F --artifact-sha256 00 --role older --json` prints 'secondary'. A consumer that routes on `command` cannot match a failure to the call it made. SPEC-44 s2 says command is the verb plus the action.
defects.proposed_fix: In `_json_envelope` accept any verb in the parser choices (cli_commands.names()) and append argv[1] when it is an action; in `_command_name` append `args.action` when a registry verb has one and no explicit nested label. cli.py is exactly at its seam budget (920 lines = CLI_BASELINE_LINES 914 + 6), so the edit must be line-neutral or bump the baseline with a bug-fix note as was done before.
defects.regression_test: tests/test_cli_registry.py::test_failure_envelope_names_verb_and_action (new; parametrized over build-env show, graph leads, strings list, diaphora show, pilot why bad --candidate, secondary binexport-check bad sha)

defects.summary: Envelope `status` values outside the vocabulary SPEC-44 s4 allows: `ok` (panels, search) and `too-broad` (search).
defects.failure_scenario: A consumer that treats any status other than complete/partial/failed/cancelled/unavailable/stale/no-results as an error rejects every successful `patchtrace search ... --json` and `patchtrace panels list --json` (both observed with status 'ok', exit 0).
defects.proposed_fix: Owner decision: either list `ok` and `too-broad` in SPEC-44 s4 as observed v1 values (additive note) or map them to `complete`/`partial` in enrichment-cli/2. Until then document them; do not change shipped values silently.

blockers.detail: Status vocabulary and the additive rule of SPEC-44 s2 (change shipped status strings or document them).

acceptance_tests: Basis: 9 acceptance items; 7 met (Qt-free dispatch; one JSON document on success; envelope on parse failure; cancelled status on exit 5; redacted errors; terminal-escaped text; registry isolates a broken verb), 2 not met (consistent command label; closed status vocabulary).

defects.summary: `kb explain`, `kb leads` and `kb export` exit 3 (runtime failure) for a project directory that does not exist; the rest of the CLI exits 2 (PT-STORAGE).
defects.failure_scenario: A script that retries on exit 3 (transient runtime failure) and aborts on exit 2 (bad input) loops forever on `patchtrace kb leads /typo/path --json` (observed: exit 3, error 'PT-KBC-STORAGE: the project cannot be opened'); `patchtrace rank /typo/path --json` exits 2.
defects.proposed_fix: Catch the 'directory does not exist / is not a project' case separately and raise PT-KBC-INPUT (already in ARGUMENT_CODES -> exit 2); keep PT-KBC-STORAGE (3) for a damaged or locked store.

remaining: No verb creates a project from two local files without a KB investigation id, a network download, or a 3-8 build series (ProjectService.create, src/patchtrace/service.py:81, has no direct CLI caller).
No verb imports an existing Ghidriff JSON (ProjectService.prepare_import/apply_import, src/patchtrace/service.py:153,251; only caller is src/patchtrace/ui.py:2814).
SPEC-44 s7 still records `project` and `import` as 'not in the alpha' proposals; the spec must be amended before the verb is added (AGENTS.md).

defects.summary: There is no headless way to turn two local binaries into an analysed project: no direct project-create verb, no Ghidriff-JSON import verb and no single-pair comparison verb.
defects.evidence: src/patchtrace/cli.py:651-676 (_run_pair is reachable only from `series create --run`); src/patchtrace/service.py:81,153,158 (create/import have no CLI caller); src/patchtrace/ui.py:1908,2755,2814 (the only callers)
defects.failure_scenario: An unattended job that holds old.dll and new.dll runs `patchtrace series create --builds old.dll new.dll --root R --run ...` and gets exit 2 'PT-NWAY-INPUT: a series needs 3-8 builds, got 2' (observed). `backend selftest` needs the bundled runtime and a function name to expect, and `kb import-pair` needs an investigation id and never runs Ghidriff. Every derived verb (rank, unified, export...) then has no completed run to work on, so the core workflow cannot be scripted.
defects.proposed_fix: Add `cli_commands/project.py` (create, info, import-json, backup) over ProjectService and `cli_commands/compare.py` over the `_run_pair` flow (tasks F-T07, F-T08), after amending SPEC-44 s7/s9.

blockers.detail: SPEC-44 s7 marks project/import as proposals 'not in the alpha'; the current directive's required CLI list supersedes that, but the spec text must change first.
A new verb needs a docs/help page and a README index line (tests/test_help_docs.py); docs/help/** is lane L6.

defects.summary: `secondary import-bindiff PROJECT FILE` reports a missing or unreadable FILE as a runtime failure (exit 3) with the message 'Could not prepare a private working folder (FileNotFoundError)', and creates runs/<id>/raw/secondary/ in the project first.
defects.evidence: src/patchtrace/secondary/bindiff.py:156-170 (_preserve mkdirs, then copy_and_hash); src/patchtrace/secondary/bindiff_inputs.py:154-157 (lstat failure -> PT-SECONDARY-RUN workdir error)
defects.failure_scenario: `patchtrace secondary import-bindiff ./proj ./typo.BinDiff` -> 'error: PT-SECONDARY-RUN: Could not prepare a private working folder (FileNotFoundError).' exit 3 (observed). The operator is told to look at disk or permissions when the path is simply wrong, and automation classifies a usage error as a runtime failure.
defects.proposed_fix: In `_preserve` (or at the top of import_bindiff when preserve_dir is set) check that the source is an existing regular file before creating the directory and raise the existing `_fail('cannot read BinDiff file: ...')` (PT-SECONDARY-INPUT -> exit 2).

actionable_now.why: F-D01, F-F03, F-F15: binary import, Ghidriff JSON import, run listing and backup are GUI-only. Wraps ProjectService.create (service.py:81), .open + project.runs/artifacts/matches (info), .prepare_import/.apply_import (service.py:153,251), .review_match (service.py:313; `rules propose` needs an accepted match) and .backup (service.py:138).
actionable_now.risk: Medium. `info` must open with maintenance=False so a read never mutates; import-json must go through prepare_import/apply_import so the pair-identity checks stay; text output must use the terminal escaping helpers. The help page and README line are inside docs/help/** (lane L6): the L6 branch does not touch README.md or page numbers above 52, so the overlap is an added file plus one added line, but it must be agreed with L6.
actionable_now.acceptance: create: exit 0, JSON result has project path, both artifact SHA-256 values and whether inputs are identical; exit 2 for a directory that already holds a project or a non-PE input. info: lists runs (id, status, backend, started), match count, revision, orientation; exit 0. import-json: exit 0 and matches present; a result for another pair exits 2 and leaves the revision unchanged. review: sets one match to a review state from the REVIEWS vocabulary, exit 2 for an unknown match or state. backup: writes a verified copy, never overwrites. notes: Method. Read-only. The real CLI was enumerated by running --help on the root and on every subcommand and sub-subcommand: 106 help pages, all exit 0, raw text in scratch:/inventory/cli-help.txt. 24 top-level verbs (11 built in, 13 from cli_commands/), 86 visible leaves in help, one real leaf that help cannot show (`kb index sync`), three hidden workers. Behaviour was probed with 109 invocations against a synthetic sample project in the scratch directory with stdin closed. The parity matrix is scratch:/inventory/parity-matrix.md (48 GUI capabilities: 23 full, 8 partial, 12 GUI-only, 5 not applicable; 19 required CLI items: 6 full, 12 partial, 1 missing; doc drift table in its section 4). Evidence. Everything here is mocked, synthetic or fixture evidence. No live-native CLI run exists in this inventory: Ghidra, Ghidriff, BinDiff, rizin, capa, FLOSS and DiE are not installed and NVD, MSRC, Winbindex and CISA are unreachable. validation_pct counts acceptance items that have a passing automated test of any offline class; it is not live compatibility evidence. Only tests/test_cli_registry.py and tests/test_help_docs.py were executed here (249 passed, 1 skipped, 2.1 s); other test files are cited from reading, not from a run. Audit follow-up. Of the findings in docs/audits/20261015-reports-cli.md and 20261015-qa-cli-persistence.md, CLI-2, CLI-3/QA-CLI-1, CLI-5/QA-CLI-3, CLI-6, CLI-7, QA-CLI-2 and QA-CLI-4 are fixed on main (verified in src/patchtrace/cli.py and by probe); CLI-1, CLI-4, CLI-12 wait for an owner decision; CLI-11, CLI-13, CLI-15 are still open; CLI-8/9/10 (reports) were not re-checked here. Constraints for implementers. (1) src/patchtrace/cli.py is exactly at its seam budget (920 lines; tests/test_cli_registry.py::test_cli_seam_budget allows baseline 914 + 6), and cli.COMMANDS must not change: a new verb is a cli_commands/<verb>.py adapter of at most 25 lines over a Qt-free feature module, with no registry line to edit (discovery is by file). (2) tests/test_help_docs.py requires a docs/help page titled `# `patchtrace <verb>`` linked from docs/help/README.md for every verb; docs/help/** is lane L6, so every new-verb task carries lane_conflict L6 for one added page and one added index line (the L6 branch does not touch README.md). (3) SPEC-44 section 7 still records project, import, doctor and config as proposals 'not in the alpha'; F-T06 amends the spec first. Lanes. No task edits backend.py, backend_cli.py, tests/test_backend_cli.py, tools/unified/**, unified/{sources,ladder,fusion,facts}/**, ui_export_v2.py or ui_inspection.py. Unverified. Windows behaviour of any verb; frozen-executable discovery of registry verbs; whether the GUI has a correlate or flags action beyond the profile fields (grep found none); whether the Rules panel can propose on a project where the CLI cannot; the earlier live acquisition probe recorded in tasks/todo.md.

summary: The real CLI has 24 verbs and 87 leaves; all have text and JSON, none prompts, and 109 probes produced no traceback. Two high-severity gaps: two local binaries cannot be imported and compared without the GUI, and `rules propose` can never succeed from the CLI. Manual correction import/export is entirely missing; profiles, runtime discovery, offline ZIP install, backup and swap are GUI-only. Three medium defects are wrong exit codes or a false "never fetches" help claim. `docs/cli-reference.md` lacks 37 of 87 leaves, and the guide lists six built verbs as not built. Deliverables: F.json, parity-matrix.md, cli-help.txt in the inventory folder. New verbs need a docs/help page (lane L6).
